react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolomics analysis reveals robust perturbation of one-carbon metabolism and connected amino-acid trans-sulfuration pathways across three independent computational paradigms. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) is the unambiguous cross-paradigm winner: it achieved rank 1 in RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 3.1×10⁻¹⁶, fold enrichment 664×), rank 1 in Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p=0.018, 8 of 8 metabolites overlapping), and consistent compound hits in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (4 metabolites: choline, L-cystathionine, O-phospho-L-serine, sarcosine). This pathway coordinates folate-dependent one-carbon transfers through S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019), a universal methyl donor whose differential abundance implicates altered methylation capacity in the treatment condition. The driver metabolites O-phospho-L-serine (C01005) and sarcosine (C00213) anchor the serine-to-glycine interconversion hub. A secondary axis of perturbation in glycerophospholipid metabolism (Mummichog rank 1, p=0.043; MetaboAnalystR p=0.02) is driven by choline (C00114) and phosphorylcholine (C00588), reflecting altered phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis or membrane turnover. L-Cystathionine (C02291) bridges the glycine/serine cluster to the trans-sulfuration pathway, linking the one-carbon and hydrogen-sulfide generation networks. The presence of (R)-lipoic acid (C16241) in the RaMP hit list extends the affected network to mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Uridine 5'-monophosphate (C00105) independently supports pyrimidine metabolism perturbation (Mummichog rank 10). Together, these findings describe a treatment-induced reprogramming of one-carbon folate metabolism with downstream consequences for methylation, membrane lipid turnover, and amino-acid trans-sulfuration.

  "narrative_text": "The differential metabolomics analysis reveals robust perturbation of one-carbon metabolism and connected amino-acid trans-sulfuration pathways across three independent computational paradigms. This pathway coordinates folate-dependent one-carbon transfers through S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019), a universal methyl donor whose differential abundance implicates altered methylation capacity in the treatment condition. A secondary axis of perturbation in glycerophospholipid metabolism (Mummichog rank 1, p=0.043; MetaboAnalystR p=0.02) is driven by choline (C00114) and phosphorylcholine (C00588), reflecting altered phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis or membrane turnover. L-Cystathionine (C02291) bridges the glycine/serine cluster to the trans-sulfuration pathway, linking the one-carbon and hydrogen-sulfide generation networks. The presence of (R)-lipoic acid (C16241) in the RaMP hit list extends the affected network to mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Uridine 5'-monophosphate (C00105) independently supports pyrimidine metabolism perturbation (Mummichog rank 10).
